flawed_step: Lines 13–16 incorrectly infer that H1 ∩ N2 is normal in H1 (and symmetrically that H2 ∩ N1 is normal in H2). The cited intersection result only yields normality in H1 ∩ H2 here.
counterexample: Let G=S3, H1=S3, N1={e}, and H2=N2={e,(12)}. Then N1 ◁ H1 and N2 ◁ H2, but H1 ∩ N2={e,(12)} is not normal in H1=S3: (123)(12)(123)^{-1}=(23), which is not in {e,(12)}. Thus line 15, subsequently cited at line 35, is false.
assessment_summary: The proof relies on an invalid normality assertion. Although the stated theorem may be recoverable using normality inside H1 ∩ H2, that argument is not what the proof gives.
